verification.description: To record whether a piece of account data has been verified, and how. Verification events are read-only and derived by the server: they accompany the data they qualify and cannot be created or updated by apps.

email.description: The verification state of the account email address. It accompanies the account email event (same stream, type `email/string`). `verified` is the answer to rely on; `method` and `verifiedAt` say how and when, and the list of methods may grow without changing what `verified` means.

verified.description: `true` only when ownership of the address was proved: the holder clicked a one-time link mailed to it (`email-link`), pasted a one-time code mailed to it at registration (`email-code`), or the platform operator marked it verified (`operator`). `false` in every other case, including an address given at registration without proof (`registration`) and an address set without proof by an earlier version of the platform (`legacy`).

method.description: How the current state was reached. `email-link`, `email-code` and `operator` come with `verified: true`; `registration` (the founding address, not proved) and `legacy` (set without proof) come with `verified: false`. `null` when no method is recorded.

verifiedAt.description: When ownership was proved, Unix timestamp (seconds). `null` when the address is not proved or the time is unknown.
